newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares slide from day-earlier high.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares slide from day-earlier high.

text.p: Swedish share prices backed down from a record high a day earlier to close more than one percent lower on Thursday.
The general index fell 1.1 percent to 3,156.91 in turnover totalling 3.8 billion crowns.

"The general view now is that most shares are expensive. A real correction will probably clear the air and make the market less paralysed," one broker said. Dealers said they would to look at Wall Street for direction.
Profit-takers brought down telecoms group Ericsson and the share fell 7.5 crowns to 359.5.

One dealer said Ericsson would probably see a sharper correction than the broad market considering its climb since posting stronger-than-expected earnings for the first half of the year. Ericsson's closing price on Thursday was some 30 crowns higher than on July 23, the day before the result.

Drug company Astra fell five crowns to 143. Rival Pharmacia & Upjohn shed five crowns to 298.5 as analysts cut forecasts by up to 10 percent after a weaker-than-expected second quarter earlier this week.
"The more people had a chance to look at it, the less they liked what they saw," said PaineWebber analyst Jeff Chaffkin.

Volvo closed 1.5 crowns higher at 213.5 after announcing it had sold its entire stake in French car maker Renault for a capital gain of 750 million crowns. Analysts said the sale was expected but the timing was good.
Appliance maker Electrolux bucked the market trend and rose 13 crowns to 616.

Swedish commercial bank S-E-Banken rose 0.50 crown to 91.50 in part because of a report in Estonia's Eesti Ekspress rumours that it had held merger negotiations with Hansapank . S-E-Banken declined to comment on the report.
